title: Task Dashboard with Async Data Fetching
description: Build a task dashboard that fetches data from a mock API, handles loading and error states, supports refresh functionality, and includes client-side filtering.
requirements: Display a loading message 'Loading tasks...' with class 'loading' while fetching data
Show error message with class 'error' if fetch fails, displaying the error text
Include a 'Retry' button in the error state that refetches data when clicked
Show a header with an h1 containing 'Task Dashboard' and a 'Refresh' button
The Refresh button should reload the tasks when clicked
Display a status filter dropdown with options: All, Pending, In Progress, Completed
The filter should have a label 'Filter by status:' wrapping both label text and select element
Filter tasks based on the selected status (show all when 'all' is selected)
Display each task in a div with class 'task-item' showing title (h3), status (span with class 'status'), and priority (span with class 'priority')
Use the provided fetchTasks function to load data on component mount
Properly handle the Task interface type for TypeScript
Use try/catch/finally for error handling with proper loading state management

browserTests.name: Filtering by pending shows only pending tasks
Filtering by completed shows completed tasks
Task items show title, status, and priority
Status spans exist in task items
Priority spans exist in task items

hints.setup: You'll need state for: tasks array, loading boolean, error string, and statusFilter string
hints.fetching: Create an async loadTasks function that calls fetchTasks() inside try/catch/finally
hints.useEffect: Call loadTasks() in useEffect with empty dependency array to fetch on mount
hints.filtering: Use tasks.filter() to create filteredTasks based on statusFilter value
hints.rendering: Use conditional rendering: if loading return loading div, if error return error div with retry button, else return dashboard
